1395:
(a) Where features of the comprehensive plan, such as school sites, parks, playgrounds or sites for other public building and open spaces, as approved by the city or county board of education, are located in whole or in part within a proposed subdivision, any portion of which lies within the city, the planning commission shall determine on the preapplication plan or the preliminary plat of the subdivision (according to the procedure being followed) the boundaries of the portions of such features included within the subdivision and shall provide for the acquisition of such public sites and open spaces according to the following provisions:
(1) Where acquisition upon the approval of the final plat is possible, this is the recommended procedure.
(2) Where acquisition is not immediately possible, the public sites and open spaces shall be reserved for a period of five years from the date of final plat approval, within which time the city or county board of education may purchase the public site or open space from the subdivider at the price previously agreed upon by the procedure specified in section 113-110(5). The subdivider shall be paid interest at the rate of six percent per annum on the amount as determined by section 113-110(5) for the sites being reserved, such interest to run for the period of time between approval of the final plat by the planning commission and termination of reservation. The reserved site should be platted in lots as part of the overall subdivision, so that in case it is not acquired, it can be efficiently used for building lots.
(b) In case there is a need for public sites or open spaces not designated on the comprehensive plan, but which are considered essential by the planning commission, the planning commission shall attempt to arrange voluntary reservation of such sites with the subdivider. The time period of reservation would, in such a case, be determined by negotiation, and although the city (county) or city (county) board of education would be under no obligation to purchase, a price to be applied in the event of purchase shall be agreed upon within 60 days of application for preliminary plat approval. The reserved site should be platted in lots as part of the overall subdivision, so that in case it is not acquired, it can be efficiently used for building lots.
(c) Due regard shall be shown to the preservation of all natural features, such as large trees, historical spots, lakes and ponds, and similar community assets, which if properly included in the overall design of the subdivision, will add attractiveness and value to the property.

(1) Streets.
a. The internal streets serving the mobile homes and complementary facilities shall have a right-of-way width of 50 feet.
b. A gridiron-type street system will not be acceptable, nor any other type of site planning which would result in a monotonous, unattractive development.
c. The park or subdivision shall abut for a distance of at least 200 feet any street upon which there are ingress and egress points.
d. Privately-owned streets shall service all lots and parcels within a mobile home park, but shall meet the improvement standards specified in article V of this chapter. Private streets shall not be permitted within a mobile home subdivision.
e. A deflection in the alignment of a service street shall be connected by a curve having minimum centerline radius of not less than 80 feet.
f. The requirement for a 100-foot tangent between reverse curves is not applicable.
g. Dead-end streets shall have an 80-foot-diameter turnaround, but the right-of-way may be the same dimension.
h. The street system within a mobile home park shall provide direct access to areas to be occupied by transient mobile homes, so that it is not necessary to pass through areas of nontransient homes in order to reach them.
(2) Easements. Utility easements (section 113-141(a)) shall not be required in a mobile home park but shall be required in a mobile home subdivision.
(3) Block. Limitations on the lengths of blocks shall not apply.
(4) Lots
a. Each mobile home lot shall have a minimum area of 2,000 square feet and a minimum width of 30 feet. Recreation areas provided for the common use of residents of the mobile home park or subdivision shall be permitted to reduce the minimum area of the mobile home lot by an area equal to the total area of the recreation areas divided by the total number of lots in the park or subdivision, such reduction not to exceed 300 square feet.
b. Each park or subdivision shall have not less than 25 mobile home lots.
c. Mobile home lots shall be so proportioned as to provide space for a mobile home stand of ten feet by 50 feet, a patio of 180 square feet, and a driveway and one automobile parking space, and shall meet any yard and open space requirements of the zoning regulations pertaining to mobile homes.
d. Parcels to be provided for commercial and service facilities shall be of size and design necessary to serve only the particular park or subdivision.
e. Minimum length of lot abutment on a public street (section 113-143(b)) shall not be required.
f. The minimum building setback provision (section 113-143(c)(4)) shall not apply.
(5) Buffer. Surrounding the park or subdivision (excepting only ingress and egress points) there shall be a planting easement of at least 15 feet upon which buildings shall not be permitted and which shall be planted and permanently maintained in trees and shrubbery that will within five years after planting, be six feet in height and obscure objects behind the easement at a distance of 50 feet. In the case of a mobile homes subdivision, an association of property owners shall be created through deed or plat covenant and shall have the responsibility of maintaining the trees and shrubbery, such association to have appropriate organization and adequate powers, as determined by the planning commission, to perform its duties.
(Ord. of 7-7-1964, § III(H))
1401:
Consistent with the overarching goals of this chapter, this division is intended to allow for private street and/or gated developments as one type of residential development alternative to allow the city to expand housing types and promote smart residential subdivision growth within the city.
(Ord. No. 08-01, § I(A), 1-15-2008)
1402:
The provisions of this division shall apply to the city, including, without limitation, portions of the city which lie in Pierce County, Georgia, and any portions which may be annexed hereafter, and further includes property which may lie in any other county of the state which is subsequently annexed into the city.
(Ord. No. 08-01, § I(B), 1-15-2008)
1405:
Unlike other developments in the city, a gated residential development, where a gate is placed at the outer periphery of the development in order to restrict access, may be allowed to have private streets that are not owned and maintained by the city. All gated residential developments must be developed in accordance with the regulations of this subdivision, other applicable regulations of this chapter, and the city's zoning ordinance.
(Ord. No. 08-01, § II(intro. ¶), 1-15-2008)
1406:
The design and layout of any gatehouse, entry gates, external fence, walls, and berms shall be located outside any public street right-of-way and shall be designed to blend in, to the greatest degree feasible, with the proposed development and be attractive to motorists and pedestrians from adjoining public streets. Gatehouses and entry gates shall be located outside any required buffer areas. Entry gates shall be set back sufficiently far from public street entrances to allow for stacking of at least three vehicles out of the public travel lanes. An additional setback between the point of the access control device and the entry gate shall be required to allow a vehicle which is denied access to safely turn around and exit onto a public street. Pedestrian access to the gated residential development shall be provided at its entrance outside of the vehicle travel lanes. Entry gates shall have sufficient minimum gate widths and openings to allow safe passage of all vehicles permitted to use public roadways. Overhead barriers or obstructions shall not be allowed above entry gates.
(Ord. No. 08-01, § II(A), 1-15-2008)
1407:
With the exception of the placement of a gate and guardhouse in a private street right-of-way, all private roads, traffic signs and markings shall meet all applicable minimum right-of-way, pavement, construction, and design standards for public roads as established by the city. The city reserves the right to have streets inspected during the construction phase to ensure that they are being built in accordance with all applicable standards.
(Ord. No. 08-01, § II(B), 1-15-2008)
1408:
Prior to the approval of a final plat, the subdivider shall submit to the city evidence that the subdivider has created a homeowners' association whose responsibility it will be to maintain common areas, private utilities, private streets, curb and gutter and sidewalks within the subdivision. Such evidence shall include filed copies of the articles of incorporation, declarations, and homeowners' association bylaws. The maintenance and upkeep of any guardhouses or entry structures, and subdivision walls, fences, or berms located at the external periphery of the subdivision as well as internal streets, curb, gutter, sidewalks and utilities shall be the sole responsibility of the subdivider and/or any duly incorporated and active homeowners' association.
(Ord. No. 08-01, § II(C), 1-15-2008)
1409:
(a) The subdivider and homeowners' association shall guarantee access to all private streets by emergency and law enforcement vehicles. Access procedures must ensure immediate access through the entry gates for emergency and law enforcement vehicles responding to emergencies. Approach and departure areas on both sides of a gated entrance must provide adequate setbacks and proper alignment to allow free and unimpeded passage of emergency vehicles through the entrance area. The subdivider shall provide documentation from city fire chief or his designee that proposed entry gates and access procedures meet all city standards for access by emergency and law enforcement vehicles.
(b) The subdivider and homeowners' association shall guarantee access to all private streets by the city, county agencies, state agencies, and all public utility companies. City, county and state officials and staff shall be permitted entry to the gated residential development to perform zoning, inspections and other governmental regulatory activities. Public utility company vehicles and personnel shall be permitted entry to the gated residential development to perform installation and maintenance activities of public utility infrastructure. A statement to this effect shall appear on or accompany the final plat.
(c) If the homeowners' association fails to maintain reliable access for the provision of emergency or other public services, the city may enter the gated residential development and open, disable or remove any gate or device, which is a barrier to access, at the sole expense of the homeowners' association. The declaration of covenants, conditions and restrictions and any other relevant documents of the homeowners' association shall include this provision.
(Ord. No. 08-01, § II(D), 1-15-2008)
1412:
The installation of the site improvements specified hereunder, or sufficient guarantee of the installation thereof, as provided by section 113-112(b), is required prior to approval of the final plat.
(Ord. of 7-7-1964, § IV(intro. ¶))
1413:
(a) Monuments shall be placed at all block corners, angle points, points of curves in streets, and at intermediate points as required by the city (county) engineer. 1414:
(a) Required paving.
(1) Pavement widths shall conform to the following:
Type of Street | Minimum Width
Connector | 40 feet or as recommended by the city engineer up to 56 feet
Service | 28 feet, curb-to-curb
Marginal access | 28 feet, curb-to-curb

(2) Paving shall be required for all service streets and marginal access streets within a subdivision any portion of which lies within the city district and shall conform to the following requirements:
a. All service and marginal access streets within areas of primarily residential use shall be properly graded and provided with a minimum of six inches of compacted, approved sand clay or soil cement base and a double surface bituminous treatment, all in accordance with city standards.
b. All service and marginal access streets serving industrial and commercial areas shall be graded and paved in accordance with city standards relating thereto.
(3) Provided that the entire right-of-way of a proposed or existing connector street (as specified by the planning commission under section 113-140(i)) has been dedicated to or purchased by the city and provided that the street provides access to adjoining lots, the subdivider shall grade and pave such street in accordance with city standards and shall be reimbursed one-half the cost of these improvements. If such street does not provide access to adjoining lots, the subdivider may be required, at the option of the city, to grade and pave such street, with reimbursement of the total cost thereof.
(4) With respect to the platted portion of a street extended past a street intersection to a subdivision boundary where the adjacent property is unplatted and which need not be opened for circulation within the particular subdivision, the planning commission may relieve the subdivider of the street improvements otherwise required thereon. Such improvements shall be installed by the subsequent subdivider of adjacent land whose street connects therewith.
(b) Grading. Regardless of whether paving is required in the particular district (section 113-141(a)), proper grading shall be carried out in accordance with the plans and data specified in section 113-111 (c); and where paving is not provided, the roadway width shall be at least 34 feet.
(c) Curb and gutter. Curb and gutter shall be required for all service streets and marginal access streets within a subdivision any portion of which lies within the city district and having a typical lot width at the building line ranging from 66 feet to 150 feet. The subdivider shall be reimbursed one-half the cost of the curb and gutter; and the city may, at the option of the subdivider, install the curb and gutter in lieu of reimbursement, such installation to be the subject of an agreement executed by both parties. Should the subdivider elect to install curb and gutter in subdivisions where it is not required, the immediately preceding provision relating to reimbursement and installation shall apply. Curb and gutter shall not be limited to any specific type but shall meet the requirements of the city engineer.
(d) Alleys. All alleys will be graded for the full 20-foot width, shall be provided with concrete aprons to all street intersections which are paved or to be paved in accordance with this chapter, and shall be properly drained, all in accordance with city standards.
(e) Street marker signs. Street name signs, of the design and material specified in city standards, shall be installed at all intersections of a subdivision any portion of which lies within the city district.
(Ord. of 7-7-1964, § IV(B); Ord. No. 08-04, § 2, 2-19-2008; Ord. No. O21-28(2), § 1, 12-21-2021)
1415:
(a) Water. A subdivision any portion of which is located within 500 feet of a public water system approved by the county health department shall be connected therewith, provided that mains within that distance can adequately serve the subdivision. Mains shall be provided by the subdivider from point of connection with the public water system to the subdivision; and all mains and service connections necessary to properly serve the subdivision shall be provided and shall be of a size that will furnish at least 15 gallons per minute to each anticipated dwelling unit, the number of dwelling units to be determined by the planning commission based upon the number of parcels for single-family and multiple-family dwelling units indicated on preliminary plat data and upon zoning restrictions (if any), and that will furnish adequate quantity and pressure for fire protection within 1,000 feet of each anticipated dwelling unit. Water lines shall conform with accepted standards of good practice for municipal water systems and shall meet, as a minimum, the specifications of the city water department and the county health department. Where a subdivision is not within 500 feet of an approved public water supply, a community water system approved by the county health department and the city (county) engineer may be provided, in which case deed or plat covenants shall establish a perpetual maintenance organization of property owners so that there is reasonable assurance of proper maintenance; or else the subdivision may be designed for individual water systems, to be installed in accordance with the standards of the county health department.
(b) Sewer. When the nearest boundary of the subdivision is located within 500 feet of public sewerage system, sanitary sewers shall be installed and connected with the public system provided that gravity flow is feasible. Mains shall be provided by the subdivider from point of connection with the public sanitary sewer to the subdivision and all mains and service connections necessary to properly serve the subdivision shall be provided. Mains shall be at least eight inches in diameter or of such larger size as may be determined by the city water department, provided that a six-inch main which is not over 400 feet in length may be permitted where topographic conditions prohibit further extension of the main; service connections shall be of four inch diameter. Where the subdivision is not within 500 feet of a public sewerage system, a community sewerage system of design approved by the county health department and the city (county) engineer may be provided, in which case deed or plat covenants shall establish a perpetual maintenance organization of property owners so that there is reasonable assurance of proper maintenance; or the subdivider may provide individual septic tanks and disposal fields, which shall meet the standards of the county health department and the city (county) engineer. The lots to contain individual septic tanks and disposal fields shall meet the minimum area requirements of section 113-143(c)(1) and (2) and may be required by the county health department to have larger areas where the results of percolation tests show that additional area is necessary.
(c) Installation of utilities. After rough grading is completed and approved and before any base is applied to the street, all of the underground work (water mains, gas mains, etc., and all service connections) shall be installed completely and approved throughout the length of the road and across the flat section. Where the utility mains are off the pavement, the developer may elect to omit the installation of service connections providing that at such time as these service connections are needed, they may be jacked across the roadway without breaking or weakening the existing pavement.
(d) Distribution of utility cost.
(1) The subdivider shall be responsible for providing and installing all water and sewer lines and connections, in compliance with subsections (a) and (b) of this section, and shall bear the entire expense subject to the following provisions relating to reimbursement by the city (county):
a. For that part of a utility main adjacent or within his subdivision, the subdivider shall be reimbursed for that portion of the cost of the main in excess of the cost of a main of adequate size for his particular subdivision.
b. For that part of a utility main which is not within or adjacent to the subdivision, the subdivider shall be reimbursed one-half the entire cost of the main.
(2) In making reimbursement under the foregoing provisions, the city (county) may, upon approval by the subdivider, install utility lines and substitute charges for such installation as a part or all of its reimbursement, such installation to be the subject of an agreement executed by both parties and specifying the amount of such charges, as determined in accordance with standard rates established by the city water department for each utility and type of construction.
(3) No private equity shall remain or rest in any water or sanitary sewer main or service connection thereof or in any drainage vehicle.
(Ord. of 7-7-1964, § IV(C))
1416:
The requirements of this chapter with respect to site improvements shall apply to mobile home parks and mobile home subdivisions, except as altered by the following:
(1) Curb and gutter and pavement. Curb and gutter or concrete edging, not reimbursable by city (county), and pavement shall be required for streets within parks or subdivisions. In each case, the paved roadway shall be centered within the right-of-way; and the roadway shall not be less in width (between curbs, where used) than the following:
Type of Street | Minimum Width
Service, with parking | 36 feet
Service, with no parking | 20 feet
(2) Accessway. A properly located curb cut (where applicable) and an accessway, for the purpose of maneuvering the mobile home into position, shall be provided on each lot within a park or subdivision and shall be at least 12 feet in width, with gradient, not to exceed eight percent.
(3) Mobile home stand. A stand for parking the mobile home shall be provided on each lot within a park in accordance with Federal Housing Administration regulations and city (county) standards.
(4) Mobile home patio. A patio shall be provided on each lot within a park or subdivision in accordance with Federal Housing Administration regulations and city (county) standards.
(5) Utilities. Each park or subdivision shall be connected with a public water or sewerage system if within 500 feet thereof; and if not within 500 feet, it shall provide its own community system or connect with a public system, such utilities to meet all provisions of section 113-230(a) and (b) applicable thereto. Septic tanks and drainage fields for individual lots shall not be permitted.
(6) Storm drainage. Where curb and gutter is used, a storm sewer system shall be provided. Where concrete edging is used, storm drainage ditches will be located at the periphery of the park or subdivision (rather than along the interior streets); and the entire site of the park or subdivision shall be graded to permit such drainage.
(Ord. of 7-7-1964, § IV(D))
